comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## RCA (Phase 1 complete — confirmed root cause)

**Mechanism.** `src/rebar/metrics/analyzers/lizard_complexity.py` `analyze` returns
`AnalyzerResult(...)` unconditionally: there is no guard on `_file_complexity` returning an
empty map. `scc_loc.analyze` has exactly that guard ("scc reported no files"); lizard does not.
So "lizard measured nothing" is encoded identically to "lizard measured zero complexity", and
the metrics registry publishes it as `complexity_summary` with `source: structural,
confidence: high`.

**Runtime proof (not static).** Against a scan root holding only files lizard does not support
(`notes.md`, `data.toml`), the real adapter returns:

    AnalyzerResult(complexity={'files': {}, 'functions': 0, 'total_ccn': 0, 'max_ccn': 0})

That is the confident zero, observed executing — exactly the polyglot client epic 839b's
adoption of lizard was meant to serve.

**Legitimacy = defect, cited.** The design invariant is stated in commit c3595f1f7e (ticket
c5b3): "A zero must mean 'measured zero', never 'measured nothing' — the fabricated
authoritative zero is exactly the failure epic 839b was created to eliminate." An existing
test, `tests/unit/metrics/test_lizard_complexity_heldout.py::test_empty_analysis_has_zero_aggregates`,
currently *asserts the defect*; it predates c5b3's invariant and is the RED oracle, corrected
to assert `Unavailable`. That is an expectation change (strengthening), not test-weakening.

**Caller-dependency gate: clear.** The single caller is `git_metrics.py:215 _lizard_analysis`,
consumed by `_structural_spec.compute`, which already branches on `isinstance(result,
Unavailable)` and returns it — the `Unavailable` path is live today via the scc and
missing-extra cases. No caller depends on the zero. Usage is incidental only.

## AC2 — jscpd inspected, and it IS the same defect (fixed under the same rule, not ruled out)

Ran real jscpd (`/opt/homebrew/bin/jscpd`) against an empty root and a two-file duplicated root
and diffed `statistics.total`:

    empty root:  {"clones": 0, "percentage": 0.0, "sources": 0, "lines": 0,  "tokens": 0}
    real root:   {"clones": 1, "percentage": 37.5, "sources": 2, "lines": 8, "tokens": 26}

jscpd's *report* distinguishes the two cases perfectly via `sources`. But `run_jscpd`
(`src/rebar/metrics/analyzers/_jscpd.py:45-52`) extracts only `clones` and `percentage`, so its
returned payload is `{"clones": 0, "percentage": 0}` in BOTH cases — the discriminating field is
read and then discarded. That is the identical fabricated zero, so it gets the identical guard
rather than a recorded exemption. No judgement call was needed: the field is present and
unambiguous.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Phase 2 complete — RED→GREEN, mutation-checked, held out

**Test (RED first).** `tests/unit/metrics/test_lizard_complexity_heldout.py` and
`tests/unit/metrics/test_jscpd_dup_heldout.py`. Three oracles, all observed failing for the
right reason BEFORE any fix existed:

- `test_empty_analysis_is_unavailable_not_a_confident_zero` — the corrected form of the old
  `test_empty_analysis_has_zero_aggregates`, which asserted the defect.
- `test_root_without_any_language_lizard_supports_is_unavailable` — the reported scenario
  driven through the REAL library, not a fake.
- `test_zero_scanned_sources_is_unavailable_not_a_confident_zero` (jscpd).

Plus `test_measurable_root_never_reports_a_zero_complexity` (AC3), green before and after —
it is a regression guard, not an oracle.

**Held out.** The three RED tests were moved OUT of the working tree before the fix subagent
was launched; it was told `tests/` was off-limits and was given only the mechanism + the
contract. It never saw the assertions. They were restored afterwards and passed — GREEN
against an oracle the fixer could not read.

**Mutation check (teeth).** Re-seeding each defect exactly — deleting the `if not files`
guard, and deleting the zero-`sources` raise — returns all three tests to RED; restoring the
fix returns them to GREEN. Refactoring litmus: every assertion is on an observable return
value (`Unavailable` vs `AnalyzerResult`), never a private name or a source grep.

**Fix.** `lizard_complexity.analyze` returns `_unavailable("lizard reported no files")` on an
empty map, with the `_LOGGER` + `_unavailable` helper pair both sibling adapters already
carry. `run_jscpd` raises on an explicit zero `sources`, reusing the existing
`ValueError` -> `Unavailable` conversion. +28 lines of non-test code, both mirroring
`scc_loc`'s guard.

**Fix-safety audit.** Restoration, not creation — no new entry point or capability, a wrong
value corrected. No new dependency (`logging` is stdlib and already used by both sibling
adapters). No test weakened — the one changed assertion is an expectation flip from the
buggy zero to `Unavailable`, which strengthens it.

**Caller sweep — all THREE `run_jscpd` callers verified, not just the two the ticket named.**
`jscpd_dup.analyze` converts `ValueError` to `Unavailable`; `git_metrics._structural_spec`
already branches on `Unavailable`; and `scripts/backfill_complexity_clone_snapshots.py`
reaches `run_jscpd` via `_measure_clone_count`, which runs inside `measure_tree`'s
`except (... ValueError ...)` and returns `None`. So the historical backfill now records "no
measurement" instead of a fabricated zero — the same invariant, applied one layer out. No
caller depended on the zero.

**Sibling sweep.** Construct axis: the tree contains exactly THREE `AnalyzerResult(`
construction sites — `scc_loc` (guarded by c5b3), `lizard_complexity` and `jscpd_dup` (guarded
here). The class is closed, not bounded. Parity axis: the rule is "a structural metric must not
publish a zero it did not measure"; the only channel is the metrics registry, and all three
analyzers now hold it.

## Cross-change interaction found and verified — change 1487 / ticket 4bf4

While running the suite I hit `test_live_clone` failing (`assert 0 >= 1`). Verified it fails
IDENTICALLY on clean origin/main, so it is pre-existing, not a regression from this change. It
is `@pytest.mark.integration` and CI never installs jscpd, so it always skipped there.

It is already being fixed independently by change 1487 (ticket 4bf4) — its fixture sat below
jscpd's default `--min-tokens 50` floor. That change touches the SAME FILE as this one, so I
checked both compatibility axes:

- **Semantic — compatible, and mutually reinforcing.** 4bf4 adds a negative control asserting
  `AnalyzerResult` with `clones == 0` for two DISTINCT files, documented as "both files clear
  the token floor, so a zero here means 'no duplication found', not 'nothing was examined'" —
  which is precisely the invariant this ticket enforces. Built its exact fixture and ran real
  jscpd: `sources: 2, clones: 0`, so this guard correctly does NOT fire and its assertion holds.
- **Textual — conflicts.** Both changes insert new functions at the same point in
  `test_jscpd_dup_heldout.py`. Verified by cherry-picking 1487 onto this branch: one purely
  additive conflict, trivially resolved by keeping both. With BOTH applied, all 12 tests in the
  jscpd + lizard modules pass, INCLUDING the two integration tests that fail today.

Whichever lands second rebases; the resolution is keep-both. Flagging so it is not rediscovered.

## Residual risk

`test_live_clone`'s skip guard checks only that jscpd is on PATH, not that it actually measured
anything — which is how a below-floor fixture went unattributed since the day it was written.
Not fixed here (it is 4bf4's ticket, and widening into it would repeat the scope mistake this
ticket exists to avoid). Recorded, not silently dropped.

## Landing status — patch set 3 on change 1488, awaiting CI

**https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1488**

- **PS1** earned **LLM-Review +1** ("PASS, 1 advisory finding, non-blocking", no inline
  comments) and **Verified +1** — the FULL CI matrix green on ubuntu py3.11/3.12/3.13 and
  macos py3.13, plus every drift/optionality/identity gate.
- **Submit was refused with a 409**: Gerrit could not auto-rebase because change 1487 (ticket
  4bf4) landed first and touches the same file. This is the exact conflict predicted and
  pre-resolved in the comment above, so it was expected, not a surprise.
- **PS2** = rebased onto 4bf4, conflict resolved keep-both. That resolution left ONE blank
  line where ruff wants two, and CI's lint job caught it — my error: I re-ran the tests after
  resolving but not `make lint`. PS2 is superseded.
- **PS3** = PS2 + `ruff format`. Locally on the exact PS3 tree: `make lint` clean,
  `make typecheck` clean (436 files), and the jscpd + lizard suites 13/13 green INCLUDING
  both integration tests. Independently, the wider targeted run was 1643 passed / 11 skipped,
  no regressions.

PS3's CI (run 31174513500) has been QUEUED for ~1 hour without starting — GitHub Actions
runner capacity is saturated by the many changes other agents are pushing concurrently. That
is an infrastructure wait, not a signal about this change: PS3 differs from the already-
Verified PS1 only by the rebase onto 4bf4 and one whitespace character.

**Ticket deliberately left `in_progress`, NOT closed** — per AGENTS.md a ticket must not close
until its change is `Verified +1` and merged, and a passing completion-verifier is not a
substitute for green CI. The worktree `/Users/joeoakhart/6067-lizard-zero` is retained (branch
`6067-lizard-zero`, commit `fa58a320d5`) since the fix has not landed.

**To finish:** wait for PS3's `LLM-Review +1` + `Verified +1`, Submit, then
`rebar transition 6067 in_progress closed`. No code work remains.

compiled_state.description:
## The defect (same class as c5b3-1b8a-08dd-40af)

Found by the ticket-c5b3 sibling sweep. `src/rebar/metrics/analyzers/lizard_complexity.py`
ends `analyze` with:

    files = _file_complexity(lizard.analyze([str(root)]), root)
    return AnalyzerResult(complexity={"files": files, "functions": ..., "total_ccn": ...,
                                      "max_ccn": max(..., default=0)})

There is no guard on `files` being empty. If `lizard.analyze` yields zero file records --
because the scan root holds no language lizard supports, because the root is empty, or because
a scan silently produced nothing -- the adapter returns
`AnalyzerResult(complexity={"files": {}, "functions": 0, "total_ccn": 0, "max_ccn": 0})`.

That is a CONFIDENT ZERO published with `confidence: high, source: structural`: a reader
concludes the repository has no complexity, when in fact nothing was measured. It is the
identical failure mode ticket c5b3 fixed in the scc adapter, in a different tool's adapter,
and the same one epic 839b-f6d2-7e1a-4051 was created to eliminate ("fabricated authoritative
zeros"). `rebar.metrics.registry.Unavailable` is the correct representation of
"measured nothing".

Not currently reproducing on this repository (lizard measures 1708 files here), which is why
it was found by sweep rather than by observation. It is latent, and it fires for exactly the
clients epic 839b's polyglot adoption was meant to serve -- a repository of a language lizard
does not support gets a confident zero rather than an honest Unavailable.

## Why it was not fixed inside c5b3

c5b3's acceptance criteria and the operator's ruling are scoped to the scc adapter and the
module-size metric. Fixing a second adapter there would have widened a bug fix past its
ticket and past its review. Filed instead, per the sibling-sweep disposition rule.

## Also worth checking in the same pass

`src/rebar/metrics/analyzers/jscpd_dup.py` returns whatever `run_jscpd` produces without
inspecting whether any file was scanned. A duplication percentage of 0 over zero scanned files
is the same fabricated zero; confirm whether `run_jscpd`'s payload distinguishes the two before
deciding whether it needs the same guard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An empty lizard file map is reported as `Unavailable`, never a zero-valued
      `AnalyzerResult` -- proven RED-first with a test that fails on the current return.
- [ ] The jscpd adapter is inspected for the same fabricated zero and either fixed under the
      same rule or explicitly ruled out with the reason recorded.
- [ ] A regression asserts a scan root that demonstrably contains analyzable files never
      yields a zero-valued complexity result.
compiled_state.title: lizard adapter reports a confident ZERO complexity when it measures no files
